idiom_name: Jakarta Messaging JMSContext with SAM-converted MessageListener (or Spring Integration Kotlin DSL)
implementation_notes: The JMS 2.0 API called from Kotlin collapses the listener into a lambda by SAM conversion - `ctx.createConsumer(queue).setMessageListener { m -> handler(parse(m)) }` - while the outbound half is `ctx.createProducer().send(queue, payload)`, so only a thin class or extension function is needed to keep JMS types out of the application. In coroutine-based services, confine the blocking JMS context to a dedicated dispatcher (withContext(Dispatchers.IO)) or move to an async Kafka/AMQP client, because suspending functions must not be invoked from the provider's listener thread. Where Spring Integration is present, its Kotlin DSL declares the same adapter as a flow (Jms.inboundAdapter / Jms.outboundAdapter).
pitfalls: JMSContext is not thread-safe; in coroutines it must be confined to one dispatcher instead of being touched from whatever thread resumes the suspension.
The SAM lambda runs on a provider thread: capturing a coroutine scope and launching into it without an explicit dispatcher leaks the JMS thread or throws.
Exceptions thrown inside the listener are swallowed by many providers, so the adapter must decide explicitly between rollback/requeue and logging.
